subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the canonical distributed Gateway/runtime design, narrow the near-term scope to subagent execution-backend placement, or reject a core distributed runtime for now?
rationale: The codebase has partial runtime and backend seams, but the requested architecture crosses product scope, security boundaries, config compatibility, session state, and channel delivery in ways automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep As Canonical RFC
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate the product/security design while allowing narrow reviewed slices such as execution placement to land under it.

options.title: Narrow To Subagent Backends
options.body: Move near-term work to the execution-backend/resource-profile track and leave full Gateway/runtime separation out of scope until later evidence appears.

options.title: Reject Core Distributed Runtime
options.body: Treat this as external orchestration/platform work unless a missing core plugin/API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep As Canonical RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate the product/security design while allowing narrow reviewed slices such as execution placement to land under it.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman is the strongest current-main routing candidate from recent session/runtime/Gateway history, even though final product ownership may involve additional maintainers.
